materials.note: wheel and rail are the same steel

wheel.profile: wheel_profile.csv: wheel surface height z_w (mm, upward) against wheel lateral coordinate y_w (mm), section through the wheel axis; z_w = 0 at the tape circle (y_w = 0); the wheel radius at y_w is r(y_w) = tape_circle_radius_mm - z_w(y_w)

rail.profile: rail_profile.csv: rail head height z_r (mm, upward) against track lateral coordinate y (mm); the rail is straight

frames.track: x along the track in the direction of travel, y lateral pointing toward the track centre (the flange side), z upward
frames.wheel_position: the wheel profile sits at y = y_w + lateral_shift and its surface at height z_w(y - lateral_shift) + vertical_position; lateral_shift and vertical_position are unknown and follow from equilibrium (no wheel roll)
frames.contact_search: the vertical separation g(y) = z_w(y - lateral_shift) + vertical_position - z_r(y); each local minimum of g is a contact point; the potential patch of a contact point is the part of the profiles between the neighbouring local maxima of g; a patch is in contact when the bodies interpenetrate there
frames.patch_plane: each patch is planar, in the plane tangent to the rail profile at its contact point; the contact angle gamma is the rail slope angle there (atan dz_r/dy, negative where the rail falls toward +y); local axes: x (travel), s = (cos gamma, sin gamma) in (y, z), n = (-sin gamma, cos gamma) pointing from the rail into the wheel
frames.patch_gap: undeformed normal separation in a patch: both profiles (wheel in its current position) rotated into the (s, n) axes, separation n_wheel(s) - n_rail(s), plus x^2 / (2 R) with R = r_i / cos(gamma), r_i the wheel radius at the contact point (the rail is straight); negative values are interpenetration
frames.elastic_independence: the patches are far apart and are treated as elastically independent half-spaces; materials are quasi-identical so normal and tangential problems decouple

kinematics.rigid_slip: rigid slip velocity of wheel material relative to the rail, divided by the speed V, at local patch coordinates (x, s): (xi - phi*s, eta + phi*x)
kinematics.rolling: steady rolling; material passes through each patch from +x (leading edge) to -x

equilibrium: the wheelset applies to this wheel a downward force Q and a lateral force Y toward -y (pressing the flange against the rail); in equilibrium the contact forces exerted by the rail on the wheel, summed over the patches and resolved in the track frame, give sum F_z = Q and sum F_y = Y. A patch force with normal component N and tangential components (F_x, F_s) contributes F_y = F_s cos(gamma) - N sin(gamma), F_z = F_s sin(gamma) + N cos(gamma)
